title: Stochastic template annealing — prompt lab notes
content:
Purpose and quick summary:
This is a loose scratchpad for the "stochastic template annealing" idea: automatically perturb few-shot templates across a schedule (temperature-like) to expose brittle model behaviors and find robust template variants. Goal: produce a small library of annealed templates + an error taxonomy so we can add checks in Optimize to detect when templates are fragile for a given model/config.

High-level hypothesis:
- Early (low-perturbation) annealing explores semantically minor changes (rewording, sentence order).
- Higher perturbation adds stronger syntactic/structural changes (instruction inversion, additional conflicting examples, token-level noise).
- Fragile templates will cause output collapse or hallucination under small perturbations; robust templates will keep semantics and task performance.

Quick definitions (working):
- template: prompt scaffolding including instructions, few-shot examples, and a final query slot.
- anneal step: an operator that applies one perturbation (see ops list below).
- schedule: sequence of anneal steps with increasing magnitude or probability.
- robustness score: composite metric across LM responses (accuracy/intent-preservation/JS divergence of token distributions).

Perturbation ops (collection):
- paraphrase-instruction: back-and-forth paraphrase of the instruction sentence (use 175B model or local heuristics).
- shuffle-examples: reorder few-shot examples (keep labels linked).
- drop-field: remove optional clarifying sentence or meta instruction (e.g., "be concise").
- synthetic-typo: inject 1–3 char typos in examples (simulate noisy user input).
- pronoun-swap: replace named entities with pronouns or vice versa.
- negative-example-insert: add an example that is subtly wrong (known failure pattern) to detect over-reliance on position.
- constraint-relax: remove a constraint (e.g., allow multiple sentences) to see if model tightness falls apart.
- role-swap: swap the role labels in an instruction pair ("assistant"<->"user") to test role-sensitivity.

Experiment plan (mini runs):
- dataset: 120 prompts from product templates (small generative summaries, intent classification, extraction). Stratify by prompt length and token budget.
- models: r-infer-3-small (quantized dev), r-infer-3-medium, hosted-open-variant-2.
- metrics: task accuracy (when labeled), semantic overlap (BERTScore/embedding cosine), diversity (distinct n-grams), token usage delta, and failure-mode flags (empty, repeated token, contradictory).
- schedule: 0 (orig), 1 (one low-perturb op per template), 2 (two ops), 3 (one medium op + one high), 4 (high noise). Run 5 seeds each (random operator order).

Sample annealed template flow (example):
Orig template:
"You are a helpful assistant. Convert the following sentence into bullet points. Example: 
Input: 'The team shipped v1 last week and started collecting feedback.'
Output: '- Team shipped v1 last week
- Started collecting feedback'
Now convert: {INPUT}"

Anneal step 1 (paraphrase-instruction):
"Act as an assistant. Turn the sentence below into concise bullets. Example: ..."

Anneal step 2 (shuffle-examples):
Move the example after the instruction to the end.

Anneal step 3 (synthetic-typo + drop-field):
Introduce a typo in the example input and remove the explicit 'concise' constraint.

Observed failure (dev run 2025-01-14):
- r-infer-3-small: output collapsed into a single sentence, lost bullet formatting 72% of the time after step 3.
- r-infer-3-medium: retained bullets, but occasionally merged list items when example had typos.
- hosted-open-variant-2: hallucinated extra context not present in the input in ~8% of cases (inserted dates).

Initial findings / heuristics:
- Templates that mention formatting explicitly ("Use bullets") are more robust to example-order and typos than those relying on example-only signal. Suggest adding a short formatting sentence as a reliable guard.
- Typo sensitivity correlates with tokenizer fragmentation: examples where typos create rare tokens cause higher variance. So prefer templates that include a canonical exemplar with correct punctuation.
- Negative-example-insert often reveals that the model uses positional priors aggressively; detection rule: if adding a wrong example flips the correct label for unrelated input, mark template as 'position-biased'.

Failure modes taxonomy (working):
- Format-collapse: model switches to streaming/paraphrase rather than requested format (bullets -> paragraph).
- Hallucination-insert: model invents facts or dates not in the prompt.
- Repeat-loop: repeated line or token looping (observed at high anneal noise).
- Label-flip: classification label flips because an inserted negative example is near end.
- Silent-failure: model returns empty or 'I don't know' more often after certain ops.

Quick notes to self (things to try next):
- Add a targeted operator that appends an explicit "EXAMPLE_END" sentinel token after each example (try soft vs explicit separators).
- Evaluate embedding stability (cosine) between orig and annealed responses; threshold for 'semantic drift'.
- Try a constrained LM decoding strategy (top-p vs temperature) to see which decoding reduces format-collapse.
- Correlate tokenizer-level OOV rate with instability; build a small precheck that scans template examples.

Metrics to log in runs (rough):
- seed_id, template_id, anneal_step, ops_list (as string), model, accuracy_pct (if label), embed_cosine_delta (float as string), format_flag (ok/collapse), hallucination_flag (ok/yes), tokens_generated (number), runtime_ms.

Operational ideas for Optimize product: 
- Add a 'template robustness' score: run lightweight annealing at registration time and surface warnings when score < threshold.
- Automatic stabilization suggestions: (1) add explicit formatting instruction, (2) include canonical exemplar, (3) add sentinel boundaries, (4) prefer shorter instruction sentence.

Open questions and unknowns:
- Does annealing identify brittle templates that manifest only at scale (e.g., heavy batching)? Need to run on Dedicated/Dedicated-quantized to check.
- How do rollouts interact? If we auto-stabilize a template, will regression happen for edge cases (precision vs recall tradeoff)?
- What's the best lightweight schedule that catches most fragile cases without blowing up compute (cost)?

TODO (short list):
- [ ] Run a 500-template sweep with 3-step schedule on r-infer-3-medium (ticket: AIINF-3421) — assigned Marcus.
- [ ] Prototype the 'sentinel' op and re-run the bullet-format task — owner: me.
- [ ] Add tokenizer OOV detector to prompt preflight checks — owner: Lena.
- [ ] Draft a short Confluence how-to for writers: 'How to make templates robust' (link back here).

Random adhoc notes (scratch):
- In experiments, swapping role labels broke extraction tasks more than generation ones — worth documenting as "role-sensitivity" category.
- For classification tasks, inserting contradictory example tends to make the LM hedge rather than flip outright — measure confidence via logprobs if available.

References and past threads:
- Slack: #prompt-lab thread on 'format collapse' (search "format-collapse-jan2025")
- Previous docs: used some ideas from 'prompt-skeletons-progressive-scaffolding' (but different approach).

End of scratchpad. Keep this as ephemeral until we have a run-summary to formalize into a PRD.

Notes to future self: when you come back, paste the top 10 most fragile templates into the Confluence page and tag the owners so we can prioritize quick wins.
